resources.title: Intro to SQL
resources.output: A set of BigQuery queries (select, group by, joins) on a public dataset, saved as a Kaggle notebook you can link on your CV
resources.why_picked: Six short lessons, each with an in-browser exercise on real BigQuery data: select, group by, order by, aliases and CTEs (As & With), and joins. Kaggle states 3 hours and no cost.

evidence.claim: Course page: 'Learn SQL for working with databases, using Google BigQuery'; 6 lessons each with a tutorial and an exercise (Getting Started, Select/From/Where, Group By/Having/Count, Order By, As & With, Joining Data); 'Hours to earn certificate 3 (estimated)'; 'No cost, like all Kaggle Learn Courses'. No update date shown.

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Databases with SQL
resources.output: A designed and queried relational database (schema, constraints, indexes, queries) as the final project, with the SQL in a GitHub repo
resources.why_picked: University course beyond SELECT: schema design, normalization, indexes, views, weekly problem sets, final project. Free to take; the certificate costs money. Harvard lists 3 to 6 hours a week.

evidence.claim: Course page: seven weeks (0 to 6) each with a problem set, plus final project; topics CRUD, relationships, normalization, joins, views, indexes, SQLite with PostgreSQL and MySQL; non-Harvard students can take it for free as OpenCourseWare; verified and professional certificates via edX are optional paid extras
Harvard Online course page: 7 weeks, 3-6 hours a week, on demand; learners can audit for free (select course materials, no certificate); a Verified Certificate costs $299

resources.title: Python для баз даних
resources.provider: Prometheus (course by Charles Severance, University of Michigan)
resources.output: A small SQLite database built and queried from Python, plus the course certificate; keep the code in your own GitHub repo to show it
resources.why_picked: Ukrainian translation of a University of Michigan course: SQL basics, many-to-many tables, SQLite from Python, auto-checked tasks. Prometheus advises taking its first three Python courses first.

evidence.claim: Course page: marked 'Безкоштовно', 6 hours of video lectures, available at any time, certificate on completion, auto-checked tasks; translated and voiced by Prometheus from Charles Severance's 'Using Databases with Python' (Creative Commons); topics SQLite3, many-to-many tables, D3.js visualisation, Google Maps API; recommends first taking the three earlier Prometheus Python courses
DOU news article (29 Nov 2024) lists the course among five new Prometheus courses (lead calls them free), duration 6 hours, SQL basics and database architecture

resources.title: Prepare and visualize data with Microsoft Power BI
resources.output: Learn badges and a path trophy on your profile; the labs run in a hosted VM, so for a CV item rebuild the report on your own dataset
resources.why_picked: Seven Microsoft modules, about 8 hours: get data, clean in Power Query, semantic model, report design, Copilot, Fabric intro. Some labs run in a hosted VM. Assumes basic data concepts.

evidence.claim: Learning path page (ms.date 2025-06-24): 7 modules, Beginner; Get started, Get data, Clean/transform/load, Configure a semantic model, Design reports, Copilot in Power BI, Fabric intro; prerequisite 'familiar with data and analytics concepts'; Microsoft's catalogue lists 492 minutes

Module 'Get data in Power BI' (ms.date 2026-06-12) has 'Exercise - Get data in Power BI', about 30 minutes, run in a provided virtual machine (limited concurrent sessions); 'Clean, transform, and load data' has a Power BI Desktop load exercise

Microsoft Learn FAQ, 'How much does the training cost?': 'Microsoft Learn training is free and available to anyone who has an interest to learn about Microsoft products.' Signing in is optional; certification exams are separate

resources.title: Tableau Free Training Videos
resources.output: Working knowledge of connecting data and building a dashboard in Tableau Desktop; apply it to your own project to produce the CV item
resources.why_picked: The vendor's own short videos. The Desktop set is 8 videos, 26 minutes: connect data, workspace, calculations, dashboards. Cloud and Prep sets add more. A start, not full training.

evidence.claim: Tableau page 'Free Training Videos': Tableau Cloud/Server set (11 videos, 31 min), Tableau Desktop set (8 videos, 26 min: connecting data, workspace, dimensions and measures, dashboards, combining data, mapping, calculations), Prep set (2 videos, 10 min)
New York University library guide links 'Tableau Free Training Videos' on Tableau's site and says 'Students can get free access to Tableau Desktop Public Edition directly from Tableau'
Boston College Libraries FAQ (last updated Feb 08, 2023) points to Tableau's training and says 'Registration is necessary before you will be given access to the training'

resources.title: Tableau Public How-To Videos and sample data
resources.output: A dashboard built in Tableau Public from the Sample Superstore data; publish a version on your own data and link it from your CV
resources.why_picked: About 20 minutes of follow-along videos on the Sample Superstore data in free Tableau Public: map, area, bar charts and an interactive dashboard. Practise on your own data after.

evidence.claim: Tableau Public Learn page: 8 how-to videos (Get Started, Connect to Data, Navigate the Workspace, Map, Area Charts, Text Table, Bar Chart, Build a Dashboard), about 20 minutes in total, using the 'Sample - Superstore' Excel data set; also Sample Data and Community Resources tabs
NYU library guide: 'Tableau Public is available for free to everyone' and links the 'Official Tableau Public How-To Videos'
University of Texas at Austin Data Lab guide lists basic tutorial videos from Tableau Public and warns: 'Do not use it for confidential or proprietary data'

resources.title: OpenIntro Statistics
resources.output: A short statistical analysis (confidence intervals, a hypothesis test, a regression) of a public dataset, with the code in a GitHub repo
resources.why_picked: Free textbook PDF (you can set the price to $0): probability, distributions, inference and regression, with a software lab per chapter in R and, from chapter 2, Python. No edition year shown.

evidence.claim: Book page: 'FREE -- OpenIntro Statistics PDF' (optional contribution; set the price to $0); nine chapters from Intro to Data to Multiple and Logistic Regression; a lab for each of chapters 1 to 9 in R (Base and Tidyverse) and other tools, Python from chapter 2; no edition year or date shown

resources.title: Аналіз даних та статистичне виведення на мові R
resources.output: The course certificate and a small R script computing a confidence interval and a hypothesis test from the course practice
resources.why_picked: Ukrainian intro to statistics: probability, confidence intervals, hypothesis tests, R from week 2. Course dated 2016, so its R tooling is dated; the statistics are not. Hours estimated.

evidence.claim: Course page: dated 17 Oct 2016, 'Безкоштовно', always available, in Ukrainian, five weeks, certificate on completion; syllabus from data types to probability, confidence intervals, p-value and hypothesis testing; 'Вступ до R' in week 2; R is the practice language; no hours stated
DOU news article (2 Jan 2025) lists the course (number 12, analytics and data) among '20 безплатних курсів' on Prometheus

resources.title: R for Data Science (2e)
resources.provider: Hadley Wickham, Mine Cetinkaya-Rundel, Garrett Grolemund
resources.output: A Quarto report analysing a public dataset in R (tidyverse wrangling plus ggplot2 charts), published on GitHub Pages
resources.why_picked: Free online R introduction by tidyverse authors: visualisation, wrangling, tidying, importing and Quarto reports. Chapters have exercises; suggested answers are published separately.

evidence.claim: Book site: 2nd edition by Wickham, Cetinkaya-Rundel, Grolemund; 'This website is and will always be free' (CC BY-NC-ND 3.0); suggested answers to exercises are linked. Chapter 'Data visualization' has four 'Exercises' sections (e.g. 'How many rows are in penguins?'); topics include visualization, transformation, tidying, import, Quarto

resources.title: Statistical Inference via Data Science: A ModernDive into R and the Tidyverse (2nd ed.)
resources.output: An R analysis with regression and bootstrap confidence intervals on a public dataset, as a reproducible report on GitHub
resources.why_picked: Teaches R from first steps through regression, sampling, bootstrapping and hypothesis tests with the tidyverse. Open-source and reproducible, second edition. Learning checks have published solutions.

evidence.claim: Book site: 'A ModernDive into R and the Tidyverse (Second Edition)', authors Chester Ismay, Albert Y. Kim, Arturo Valdivia, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, dated September 21, 2026; 11 chapters from Getting Started with Data in R through regression, sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing; appendix of learning check solutions

resources.title: Fundamentals of Data Visualization
resources.output: Redrawn versions of two or three weak charts from a public report, with a short note on why each design choice was made
resources.why_picked: Tool-independent rules for chart types, colour and layout. The online text is the author manuscript before copy-editing; the book is published by O'Reilly and its source is on GitHub.

evidence.claim: Book site: author Claus O. Wilke, published by O'Reilly, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; website holds the complete author manuscript before final copy-editing; parts on amounts, distributions, proportions, relationships, uncertainty, figure design, colour pitfalls, storytelling; source on GitHub; no date shown

resources.title: Data Visualization
resources.output: A Kaggle notebook with line, bar, scatter and distribution charts built in seaborn, answering a question about a real dataset
resources.why_picked: Four hours of seaborn exercises in the browser: line charts, bar charts and heatmaps, scatter plots, distributions, plus a final project. Basic Python helps. No update date is shown.

evidence.claim: Course page: 8 lessons (Hello Seaborn, Line Charts, Bar Charts and Heatmaps, Scatter Plots, Distributions, Choosing Plot Types and Custom Styles, Final Project, Creating Your Own Notebooks); 7 with exercises; 'Hours to earn certificate 4 (estimated)'; 'No cost, like all Kaggle Learn Courses'; instructor Alexis Cook; no update date shown

resources.title: A/B Testing
resources.output: A written experiment design (hypothesis, metrics, sample size, analysis plan) for a product change, as a one-page case study
resources.why_picked: Five lessons by three Google instructors: metrics, policy and ethics, designing and analysing an experiment. Free. No duration on the page; hours are our estimate.

evidence.claim: Course page: 'Free Course', Beginner, 'Updated: May 23, 2025', no prerequisites listed, 5 lessons (overview, policy and ethics, choosing metrics, designing an experiment, analysing results), instructors Carrie Grimes, Caroline Buckey and Diane Tang (Google); no duration stated; Trustpilot 4.6 from 68 reviews is below our rating threshold so no rating is used

resources.title: Analytics Academy courses on Skillshop
resources.output: Skillshop course completions and, if you pass, the Google Analytics Certification listed on Skillshop; pair with the demo account for a portfolio sample
resources.why_picked: Google's own free GA4 e-learning: four courses, beginner to advanced, plus a certification, on Skillshop (Google sign-in). Course lengths and certification price not seen; hours is an estimate.

evidence.claim: Analytics Help 'Enroll in Analytics Academy courses on Skillshop': 'free e-learning courses'; 101 Get started (Beginner), 102 Manage GA data and read reports (Beginner), 201 Dive deeper (Intermediate), 301 Use GA with other tools (Advanced), plus Google Analytics Certification; no certification price stated
Analytics Help article '[GA4] Analytics Academy': 'a collection of free e-learning courses' on Skillshop; 'currently offers 4 training courses and a certification'

Skillshop home page has a Google Analytics section: 'Learn Google's measurement tools to help grow your business through intelligent data collection and analysis'; the catalogue host lists 'Google Analytics Certification (2026)' and requires sign-in with Google to open courses

resources.title: Google Analytics demo account
resources.output: A written analysis of the demo store's traffic sources and conversion paths, as a portfolio sample
resources.why_picked: A working GA4 account with data from the Google Merchandise Store and the Flood-It! app; explore its reports without owning a website. Pair it with the Skillshop courses.

evidence.claim: Analytics Help article 'Demo account': a fully functional Google Analytics account any Google user can access, with Google Merchandise Store (web) and Flood-It! (app and web) properties; Viewer role only; report and exploration export is not available

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Programming with Python
resources.output: A final Python project plus weekly problem sets, with the code in a GitHub repo
resources.why_picked: University beginner course, no experience needed: functions, loops, exceptions, unit tests, libraries, file I/O, problem sets, final project. Certificates are paid. Harvard lists 3 to 9 hours a week.

evidence.claim: Course page: ten weeks (0 to 9) plus final project; functions, conditionals, loops, exceptions, libraries, unit tests, file I/O, regular expressions, object-oriented programming; for students with or without prior programming experience; free to take as OpenCourseWare; verified or professional certificates are on edX

Harvard Online course page: 10 weeks, 3-9 hours a week, on demand; learners can audit for free (select course material, no certificate); certificate prices shown on the page are inconsistent ($219 and $299), so no price is recorded

resources.title: Python
resources.output: A Kaggle notebook of solved Python exercises you can link as practice evidence
resources.why_picked: Seven short lessons with exercises on syntax, functions, conditionals, lists, loops, strings and using libraries. A quick base before pandas and data work.

evidence.claim: Course page: 'Learn the most important language for data science'; 7 lessons each with a tutorial and an exercise; 'Hours to earn certificate 5 (estimated)'; 'No cost, like all Kaggle Learn Courses'; leads on to Pandas and Intro to SQL; no update date shown

resources.title: Pandas
resources.output: A Kaggle notebook that loads, selects, groups and merges a real dataset with pandas
resources.why_picked: Six lessons of short coding exercises: reading data, indexing, grouping, sorting, missing values, combining. Needs basic Python. No update date is shown; check against current pandas docs.

evidence.claim: Course page: 'Solve short hands-on challenges to perfect your data manipulation skills'; 6 lessons each with a tutorial and an exercise; 'Hours to earn certificate 4 (estimated)'; 'No cost, like all Kaggle Learn Courses'; builds on Kaggle's Python course; no update date shown

resources.title: Python for Data Analysis, 3rd edition
resources.output: A cleaned and analysed public dataset in a Jupyter notebook, with the code and data on GitHub
resources.why_picked: Written by the author of pandas: loading, cleaning, wrangling, aggregation and time series, with code and datasets on GitHub. Covers pandas 2.0, so a few newer 3.x details differ.

evidence.claim: Book site: 3rd edition by Wes McKinney, open-access HTML version, 'updated for pandas 2.0.0' and Python 3.10, update dated April 12, 2023; code examples MIT-licensed with datasets on GitHub

resources.title: 10 minutes to pandas
resources.output: A short notebook reproducing the guide's selection, grouping, merging and time-series examples on your own dataset
resources.why_picked: Official, current quick tour (docs for pandas 3.0.6): Series, DataFrame, selection, missing data, merge, groupby, pivot tables, plotting. A reference to code along with; it has no exercises.

evidence.claim: Official pandas documentation page '10 minutes to pandas', pandas 3.0.6 documentation; sections on data structures, selection, missing data, merge, grouping, reshaping and pivot tables, time series, plotting, CSV/Parquet/Excel I/O; runnable examples shown as IPython sessions, no exercises
